hero.title: Unity for dignity — the voice of private social service providers.
hero.description: PFPSS brings together professionals from Romania's private residential elderly care sector. Through advocacy, collaboration and education, we support providers in their effort to deliver services at the highest European standards.

mission.title: Our mission
mission.description: We actively support private providers in the social assistance sector, offering them a platform for expression, valuable resources and networking opportunities. We strive to be the central pillar for our members in interactions with authorities, government agencies and international partners, advocating for an optimal legislative environment and recognition of the vital contribution of the private sector to social assistance in Romania.

vision.title: Our vision
vision.description: We envision a Romania where quality access to social assistance is guaranteed for all, regardless of the difficulties faced. Through unity, innovation and unwavering commitment, we reshape the social assistance landscape to respond efficiently and flexibly to the real needs of the community.

commitment.title: Our commitment
commitment.description1: At PFPSS we believe that the dignity of every person is a fundamental right. Under the motto "Unity for Dignity", we promote and protect this principle in all our activities. In a world where social challenges become increasingly complex, unity among providers is the key to a high standard of care for the most vulnerable members of the community.

0.title: Removal of ISU authorization from the mandatory documents for licensing residential social services
0.description: Petition of residential social service operators in Romania — homes for the elderly and centres for adults with disabilities — to amend art. 12 para. (2) let. k) of Law no. 197/2012.
0.fullText:
Through this petition, we request the Ministry of Labour, Family, Youth and Social Solidarity to amend art. 12 para. (2) let. k) of Law no. 197/2012 on social assistance, by removing the operating authorization issued by the General Inspectorate for Emergency Situations (ISU) from the list of mandatory documents for obtaining the operating license for residential social services.

This requirement generates duplication of authorization procedures, significant additional costs for private providers and delays in the operation of care centres — without effectively contributing to the quality of services or the safety of beneficiaries, which is already regulated by other normative acts.

Removing this requirement will allow faster opening of new care places, reduce bureaucracy and direct resources towards the effective quality of services provided.
0.target: Ministry of Labour, Family, Youth and Social Solidarity
0.legalRef: Law no. 197/2012, art. 12 para. (2) let. k)
